Bloom Procurement Services Ltd

NEPRO3

NEPRO3 is an innovative and modern solution for the procurement of professional services. It's also the only solution of its kind within the UK's public sector marketplace.

The NEPRO3 solution

The NEPRO3 framework provides a compliant UK public sector route to market via framework call-off. It makes it easy for public sector organisations to buy and manage specialist professional services, and from a diverse range of regional and national suppliers.

Buyers are provided with considerable versatility, and substantial savings. On average, buyers using the NEPRO3 solution achieve an average saving of 14% against budget.

NEPRO3 is also an ideal solution for suppliers, making otherwise inaccessible opportunities to work alongside the public sector available. This is especially the case for SMEs and VCSES (voluntary, community, and social enterprises).

Once suppliers are registered and accredited with NEPRO3, they'll no longer face time-consuming pre-qualification stages – allowing them to compete fairly with larger suppliers.

Key categories of spend

Our Marketplace provides comprehensive access to professional services, including 20 categories and over 380 subcategories of spend.

Place

Place categories include professional services that involve the built environment, addressing everything from simple surveys to multi-disciplinary team projects.

Technology

Access the expertise needed to guide and accelerate your organisation's digital journey through our Technology category.

People

Our People categories focus on the areas that have a direct impact on the end users of public services, including those in the social care, safeguarding & health, and wellbeing sectors.

Medium Construction Works Framework. Term end: January 2027. Total Lots: 4. This fully PCR compliant framework can be used to commission a full range of building works, valued between £50k – £10m.

Major Construction Works Framework. End date: October 2026. Total lots: 3. Access the right contractors and get best value for large scale construction projects, through the Pagabo National Framework for Major Construction Works.

Civil Engineering & Infrastructure Framework. Term end: June 2026. Total lots: 4. Our Civil Engineering and Infrastructure Framework allows you to quickly and easily procure the right contractors for your next road, rail and maritime, water, nuclear or power project.

Decarbonisation Solutions Framework. End date: April 2028. This compliant framework can be used to commission a full range of building works. Providing real value and competition, the framework is divided into four main lots by value band, with each lot further subdivided in to 12 sub-lots by geographic area, giving a total of 48 sub-lots.
Developer-Led Framework. End date: October 2026. Total lots: 9. Running until October 2026, the framework is the first and only of its kind in the UK.

Professional Services Framework. End date: April 2028. The framework is split into 23 different lots, with Lot 1 a national provider appointment and Lots 2-23 individual appointments. Quickly and easily procure the right consultants and professional services for your next construction or development project.

Professional Services Framework for Scotland. End Date: April 2028. The framework has 4 dedicated lots, with Lot 1 for national providers and Lots 2–4 for regional experts. Easily source trusted consultants and professional services for your next construction, development or estates project. Our fully compliant, flexible procurement framework simplifies the process, helping you save time and ensure quality.

Decarbonisation Solutions for Healthcare Framework. End date: April 2028. This framework is dedicated to healthcare schemes, with Great Ormond Street Hospital serving as the healthcare sector-specialist contracting authority.

Mechanical & Electrical Solutions Framework. End date: August 2027. 3 lots, each covering 4 sub lots. Access a range of specialist M&E contractors and benefit from streamlined public sector procurement for all of your mechanical and electrical projects.

Demolition and Land Remediation Framework. End date: May 2026. Total lots: 5. Looking to redevelop existing estate stock or develop on brownfield sites? Our framework can help with access to contractors with expertise in both demolition and land remediation.

Refit and Refurbishment Framework. End date: May 2027. Total lots: 5. Access specialist contractors to convert buildings whilst keeping the same structure; improving and restoring buildings through renovation or incorporate the very latest in modern systems, through retrofit.
Furniture Solutions Framework. End date: April 2026. Total lots: 6. Benefit from value for money and the right supplier for all your furniture, with this national, multi-vendor framework.
Academy Services Framework. Until June 2027. Total lots: 9. The framework includes a range of back-office requirements, specifically chosen to assist academies within England.

Building Improvement Works. Like all frameworks from Fusion21, the Building Improvement Works Framework is run by technical specialists and will only feature pre-qualified, accredited supply partners. The framework offers a wide range of internal and external improvement works from the installation of kitchens, bathrooms, windows and doors to roofing work. It has been enhanced to include four new dedicated lots covering damp and mould, external environmental improvements, insulation, and aids and adaptations. Framework start date: 04/01/2024. Framework end date: 03/01/2028. A total of 9 lots are available on this framework. Worth up to £346m over a four year period. Lot 1: Kitchen and Bathrooms. Lot 2: Windows and Doors. Building Safety & Compliance. This framework has been developed to help public sector organisations meet the building compliance needs of Members and to help them maintain safe buildings. It addresses the emerging fire safety requirements of the Building Safety Agenda and includes new lots to achieve this. Framework start date: 28/04/2025. Framework end date: 27/04/2029. Worth up to £800m over a four year period. Lot 1: Asbestos Surveying & Consultancy. Lot 2: Asbestos Abatement & Removal. Lot 3: Legionella & Water Hygiene Consultancy. Cleaning & Washroom Services. Fusion21's national dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for Cleaning and Washroom Services offers a full provision of cleaning services from integrated packages to specialist services. This DPS provides a flexible and efficient procurement solution for Fusion21 Members to save money and generate social value. Scope of DPS. The DPS will remain open for new suppliers throughout its duration - allowing local suppliers, nominated suppliers or Members incumbent suppliers to be added to the tender process. DPS start date: 01/03/2021. DPS end date: 07/02/2027.

Construction Consultancy Services Framework (CCSF). This framework provides a streamlined avenue for sourcing construction-related Consultancy Services for the built environment. This framework covers surveying, stock monitoring and appraisal, environmental, architectural, engineering, project management and multi disciplinary work. Framework start date: 22/09/2025. Framework end date: 21/09/2029. A total of 15 lots including 3 new lots: Clerk of Works - Inspection Regime, Retrofit & BSA Principal Designer and Building Control. Telecommunications framework. Providing managed transmission services and dark fibre through a compliant route to market, saving you time and money. About the telecommunications framework. This framework offers you the option to direct award to the first-ranked supplier or to run a mini competition against your specific requirements. The agreement is divided into two lots. Lot one: managed transmission services. This can include: Leased circuits, Wide area ethernet, xDSL, Dark fibre. Suppliers: Neos Networks Limited (first ranked supplier; direct award and mini competition), ITS Technology Group Limited (mini competition only), Telcom Networks Limited (mini competition only). Lot two: dark fibre. Dark fibre is for customers requiring individual orders. Framework benefits: Compliant with UK procurement legislation, saving you time on running a full procurement process. The framework is open to higher education institutions, further education and specialist colleges and research council establishments in the UK.

Janet txt framework. A secure SMS messaging service to manage and distribute messages to individuals or groups. About Janet txt. Janet txt's basic service is free to set up, with no annual or monthly charges. We have re-procured this service to take advantage of the changing SMS market and have set up a new multi-supplier SMS framework agreement for the Jisc community. Following rigorous OJEU rules, we have managed to reduce unit prices, bringing you a high quality, competitively-priced service. Multi-supplier framework. Janet txt is a multi-supplier framework. Your institution can either award the contract directly to the first-ranked supplier (Commify UK) or run a mini-competition against your specific requirements with all the suppliers on the framework. The three suppliers are: Commify UK - top-ranked supplier (direct award), Critico (formerly PageOne) - framework supplier, Reach-interactive - framework supplier. Janet txt is available to the research and education community.

OCRE 2024 cloud framework. An EU-compliant procurement framework for cloud infrastructure as a service (IaaS), platform as a service (PaaS) and associated software as a service (SaaS). By purchasing services via the OCRE (Open Clouds for Research and Education) 2024 framework you get predictable, safe and cost-effective access to a portfolio of cloud providers. The OCRE 2024 framework is the latest iteration in GEANT's flagship series of public cloud frameworks. It aims to simplify the procurement process so you can find the EU-compliant solution you need. Higher education institutions, further education colleges and Research Council establishments in the UK are eligible to use the framework. Jisc applies a 3.5% administration fee for using the framework. Selection of supplier: by using the framework, you can make a direct award to any top-ranked supplier. Alternatively, a mini-competition may be run to compare the suppliers for any given platform or across all platforms. Jisc is the operator of the OCRE 2024 framework for the UK.

Data centre services. Save money, improve energy efficiency and get the scalability you need by moving systems and services to off-site data centres. About the services. We offer two distinct but complementary data centre services to eligible members and customers. You can purchase from either service or both. Shared data centre service. Two off-site facilities are available under the shared data centre framework, hosted by: Virtus, from its London4 facility in Slough; aql, from its DC5 facility in Leeds. Data centre referral service. One off-site facility is available under the data centre referral agreement, hosted by: Kao Data, from its campus in Harlow. These services are included within the scope of our ISO9001 certificate.

Digital preservation systems dynamic purchasing system (DPS). Save time and effort with an easy, fast and compliant route to acquiring a digital preservation system to suit your organisation's needs. About the digital preservation DPS. Our service enables you to purchase a digital preservation solution from pre-qualified vendors who conform to sector standards around the long-term access and preservation of your digital assets. Compliant route to market. The service was procured under Public Contracts Regulations 2015 and remains compliant under the Procurement Act 2023. A dynamic purchasing system. Open to new applications meaning new vendors and technology can join the service at any time helping to keep prices competitive. The vendors who are currently accepted on to the service are: Arkivum Limited, Artefactual Systems Inc., Docbyte NV, Ex Libris (UK) Ltd, Infotel UK Consulting, ITHAKA Harbors, Libnova S.L.U, Max Communications Ltd, Preservica Limited, Sword Ping Network Solutions.

Research management systems DPS. Save time when purchasing a CRIS or repository for the management and sharing of your organisation's research. About the service. Our service enables you to purchase a repository or current research information system (CRIS) from pre-qualified suppliers who conform to sector priorities around the management of research activities. Our stringent processes comply with EU procurement rules so you can rest assured that the suppliers chosen will provide you with the best value and quality of service. Procured in accordance with The Public Contract Regulations 2015. The service is a compliant route to market. Contact rms-support@jisc.ac.uk for a copy of the contract notice 2024/S 000-003275. Dynamic supplier list. New suppliers can join at any time during the lifetime of the DPS, ensuring that you have access to the latest technology. The DPS can be used by higher and further education institutions, specialist colleges and research council establishments in the UK.

Electronic research and laboratory notebook DPS. An easy, fast and compliant route to acquiring an electronic research and laboratory notebook that suits your organisation's needs. About the service. The electronic research and laboratory notebook is a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) which can help you purchase electronic research and laboratory notebook (ERN) products from approved suppliers. ERNs are digital tools designed to replace traditional paper lab notebooks. The DPS is Public Contracts Regulations 2015-compliant. Benefits: Allowing new suppliers to join at any time, which ensures ongoing competition and gives immediate access to innovation in the market. The DPS can be used by higher and further education institutions, specialist colleges and research council establishments in the UK.

Certificate framework. Purchase your certificates through our single-supplier framework for flexibility, compliance and sector-negotiated rates. Our certificate service helps education, public sector and not-for-profit organisations keep web and email services secure, so confidential data can be sent safely via the internet. A new route to order. We operate as a single-supplier procurement framework, with DigiCert as the new provider of the certificate service. This means you can purchase certificates directly from DigiCert under terms negotiated by Jisc. Compliance and security: supplier capability has been fully assessed as part of our procurement due diligence, and the process is fully compliant with the Procurement Act. This framework only covers the purchase of digital certificates from DigiCert.

Telephony DPS. Our Telephony DPS service retired on 1 June 2026. This service enabled organisations to procure telephony services and equipment including handsets, system support, mobile services, legacy voice connectivity (eg ISDN circuits) and SIP trunking, from pre-qualified suppliers connected to the Janet Network. Service retirement does not impact existing contracts. Agreements placed through the DPS will continue as normal and so no immediate action is required. Once your current agreement comes to an end, you may choose to procure telephony services through an alternative framework or supplier direct routes, in line with your procurement policies.

About us - Everything ICT. Everything ICT operate fully compliant frameworks that make buying ICT clear, simple, and great value for schools, trusts, and public sector organisations. Originally designed for schools, our frameworks are now trusted by many other public sector customers. Everything ICT is a DfE-approved, fully compliant procurement framework designed to make ICT purchasing simple, secure, and great value for schools and MATs. WCL (UK) Ltd, trading as Everything ICT, act as a Neutral Vendor and manage the day-to-day operation of framework agreements which have been awarded to us by E2BN (East of England Broadband Network) and HEART Academies Trust. These frameworks are: Publicly accountable; Built for education; Trusted by schools, MATs and public bodies nationwide. WCL (UK) Ltd (TA Everything ICT) Registration number: 07689604 Registered address: 124 City Road, London EC1V 2NX VAT registration: GB117509030. The framework covers the following categories: Hardware, Infrastructure, IT Support, Connectivity, Cloud Services, Consultancy, Software.

Framework Transition Info - Everything ICT. HEART Academies Trust framework transition information. As we prepare for the transition from the E2BN framework to the new HEART Academies Trust framework, we've brought together the key information and resources you'll need to understand what's changing and what it means for you. About the transition: The Everything ICT Framework is moving from E2BN to HEART Academies Trust. This is a planned and standard process, designed to keep your procurement experience seamless and compliant. All contracts awarded on or before 19 July 2026 under the current E2BN framework will continue to be fully protected and supported, with no change to delivery or service. We expect the new HEART Academies Trust framework to be in place before the current one expires, so you can be confident there will be no disruption to your procurement, contracts, or ongoing support. About HEART Academies Trust: HEART Academies Trust is the new framework authority for Everything ICT.

United Kingdom: "Everything ICT" - full range of ICT Products, Solutions, Services and Support for the public sector. Reference: FTS/018207-2022. Advanced Procurement for Universities & Colleges (APUC) is Scotland's Procurement Centre of Expertise for Universities and Colleges. APUC Ltd, Unit 27, Stirling Business Centre, Stirling, FK8 2DZ. Incorporated in Scotland: SC314764. APUC operates as a procurement consortium supporting Scotland's universities and colleges sector, putting in place collaborative framework agreements for its member client institutions.

HEPCW Agreements. Details of HE Sector collaborative agreements available to HEPCW members can be found from the drop down lists below. For further information regarding the use of each agreement including Buyers Guides, price lists etc, please visit https://www.hecontracts.co.uk/

Audio Visual. The Audio Visual Group has nine members – two from procurement and the remainder are specialists in the Audio Visual/Media centres of their institute. Those members who do not have representation are kept up to date via this site, UniBuy, meeting minutes and email. The group currently manages an inter-regional agreement for the Supply and Installation (inc. design) of Audio Visual Equipment, which commenced on 1 February 2015, for a period of 2 years, with an option to extend for 2 further 1 year periods. It also participates in other inter-regional and national agreements which can be found on UniBuy.

Catering. The Catering Group comprises the Heads of Catering from all the HEPCW member institutions, together with 3 procurement advisors, and meets every 6 to 8 weeks. The current portfolio of HEPCW Catering contracts includes: fresh fruit & vegetables; fresh meat & poultry; frozen and ambient foods; sandwiches and sandwich fillings; confectionery; savoury products; Welsh-branded produce; disposable products; counter-top vending equipment and supplies; detergents and equipment maintenance contracts. The group also has a number of nominated supplier arrangements for specialist foods and services.

Buyers Guide. One of the benefits of HEPCW membership is access to a wide range of collaborative procurement arrangements. These include agreements set up by the HE Sector, pan-UK agreements and All Wales agreements. Links to these are provided below: HE Agreements; Pan-UK Agreements; All Wales Agreements. Please note that the links above may require login to access information for individual agreements. The HE Sector contracts database is only available to users within the sector, and external stakeholders are not able to create a log in.
